title: The Book of Rites, Part I
dateDisplay: Compiled c. 5th century BCE–1st century CE
attributionNote: The Li Ki is a compilation of separate treatises on ritual, government, music and cosmology, drawn from the older texts on rites and edited in the Han; it is not the work of a single author and is not the ritual code it was once taken for.
description: The Book of Rites is the great description of Chinese religious and social practice: the rules of propriety and their meaning, mourning and its grades, the monthly ordinances, the state of equilibrium and harmony, royal regulations, the evolution of rites, music, and the conduct of the scholar. Its chapters on the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean were lifted out to become two of the Four Books. This first volume carries books I to X.
historicalContext: The compilation was numbered among the Five Classics and shaped the ritual practice of the imperial state. Legge translated the whole of it, with the Chinese text, for the Sacred Books of the East, volumes 27 and 28 (1885).
availabilityNote: Complete: books I to X in Legge's translation, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed book per chapter. The translator's long introduction and his notes are volume apparatus and are not part of the work.
